chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one performing Itikaaf in Makkah may pray in whichever of its houses he desires, and the one performing Itikaaf elsewhere may not pray except in the Masjid which he has specified.

key_terms.الْمُعْتَكِفُ: The one performing Itikaaf (spiritual retreat in a mosque)
key_terms.بُيُوتِهَا: Its houses (referring to the houses around the Kaaba used for Itikaaf)

ai.seo_question: Where should a person pray while performing Itikaaf in Makkah versus other cities?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisprudential distinction between the unique status of Makkah, where the entire city is considered a sacred space allowing flexibility in prayer locations during Itikaaf, and other cities where the retreat is strictly confined to the designated mosque. This ruling reflects the broader Shia legal principle that the sanctity of Makkah transcends specific architectural boundaries, whereas elsewhere, the validity of Itikaaf is tethered to the specific place of residence chosen by the worshipper.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one performing Itikaaf in Makkah can Pray in whichever of its house he so desires to, and the one performing Itikaaf somewhere else cannot Pray except in the Masjid which he has specified’.
en.sarwar: 5. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

One who performs ’Ttikaf in Makkah can perform Salat (prayer) in any of its houses that he chooses, and one performing ’Ttikaf in other places cannot perform Salat (prayer), unless it is the Masjid which he has determined.’”
